2052.context: However, the true measure of a belief's value is not whether it feels comforting or provides a sense of certainty. The real question we must ask ourselves is whether our belief makes us more honest and more open to correction. Does it reduce the harm we cause to others and does it improve how we treat real people in the real world? When we audit our beliefs through the lens of their real world impact, we move away from just having an opinion and toward a more ethical, evidence-based way of belonging.
